name_reason: Already fully compliant with the global naming convention: data_fd2_ prefix, battle core-table domain, descriptive body, and reflects the data type (per-slot int array). 'variant_a' is a real discriminator (parallel variant-B arrays exist at 0x54034); '6slot' is the meaningful 6-element dimension; 'color_idx' names the contents. No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix equal to its own or any data address). Nothing to change.
purpose: Per-slot color index for the variant-A 6-slot summon-spell animation (one int32 per slot, 6 slots); selects each slot's vertical row offset from the per-color row-offset table.
logic_summary: Zero-bss runtime state owned by fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_a_6slot @ 0x269D3. INIT (state_code==0) seeds slot i with color_idx[i] = i. In TICK frames (state 2/5/8) color_idx[i] indexes the local per-color vertical row-offset table (copied from data_fd2_battle_summon_anim_variant_a_10color_y_offset_table @ 0x524A8) to position the slot's sprite; when a slot's frame counter wraps at frame 8 (and the terminate flag is clear), color_idx[i] is overwritten with (rotation_counter % 10), advancing the color cycle. Values stay in 0..9.
element_semantics: Each element is the int32 color index (0..9) for one of the 6 animation slots; used as the index into the per-color vertical row-offset table.
notes: Ghidra DataType confirms int[6] (len=24). 3 xrefs all from fd2_tick_summon_anim_variant_a_6slot: writes at INIT (color_idx[i]=i @ 0x26A4E region) and frame-8 wrap (=rotation_counter%10), read in TICK as table index; game writes the array so is_const=false despite .object2 block showing write-perm=false (LE-layout artifact). Initial memory all zero (runtime-initialized). src comment block (lines 13-22) already precise/correct/ASCII; left unchanged. Ghidra data comment is stored in the PRE field (not PLATE) and is accurate and consistent with src, so left as-is. No logic issue for this symbol (its INIT path is a plain color_idx[i]=i; the RNG-vs-loop-index nuance noted in the owner function concerns the separate jitter_byte_array @ 0x54014, not this symbol).
